messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: High error rate detected for ILB controlplane -> forwarding-rules GCP API calls affecting Private VPC cross-region route propagation. Threshold breached: 5xx > 10% for 6m. Pager: alice (oncall).

alice (oncall): seeing 502/503 spikes from gcp-forwardingrules in us-eu fanout path. Private VPCs report route suppression and some customers in EU can't reach hosted endpoints. I'm jumping in.

bob (network-eng): noted similar in/egress telemetry. Looks like controlplane retries have increased and we're seeing rate limit 429s from forwarding-rules with internal backoff. Not obviously our ILB config change.

alice (oncall): quick evidence:
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/xxxx/global/forwardingRules?filter=status!="OK"
HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
{"error":{"code":503,"message":"Service temporarily unavailable"}}
```

alice (oncall): Impact: ~18 Private VPC customers with cross-region failover rules affected, degraded connectivity between eu-west and us-central. No data plane drop for single-region, but cross-region failover and new route propagations failing.

dave (customer-success): I'm getting inbound messages from 3 enterprise customers in EU complaining about 502s in their services. Drafting an incident note and customer-scoped mitigation steps. Need an ETA for a wide mitigation.

carol (sre): are we auto-failing to sibling model? Check routing policy -- we should have fallback to local region if propagation fails. If not, we toggle prefer-local routing for impacted projects.

alice (oncall): confirm some customers were pinned to cross-region priority groups so they experienced blackholes. I'm enabling temporary route fallback for those projects now.

bob (network-eng): opening ticket with GCP support, attaching spike graphs and request to escalate to networking API team. ticket: 1234567890 (gcp-support-bot please keep an eye).

gcp-support-bot: Ticket 1234567890 created. Estimated initial response: 15–30m. Linked incident: https://status.cloud.google.com/incidents/abc123 (reported: forwarding-rules API partial outage).

alice (oncall): mitigation actions in flight:
- enable prefer-local routing for affected proj ids: proj-alpha, proj-bravo, proj-charlie
- trigger explicit route re-propagation job for EU clusters
- increase healthcheck logging to capture ILB status changes
- contact CS for customer comms (dave)

eve (infra): FYI we had a small forwarding-rules rollout earlier today at 03:12 UTC that only targeted canary seeds. Rollout status shows green, but need to confirm no unintended traffic patterns hit GCP controlplane.

bob (network-eng): running quick check to see if our clients are hammering the API with retries:
```
# sample query of recent controlplane calls
select count(*), code from controlplane_api_calls where api="forwardingRules" and ts > now() - interval '10 minutes' group by code;
# result: 12000 x 503, 4500 x 429, 300 x 200
```

alice (oncall): ok that's a lot of 503s. I'll rate-limit retries for forwardingRules to aggressive backoff immediately (reduce retry window to 30s, add jitter). Patch applied to runtime.

carol (sre): pre-handoff checklist: have we documented affected customer list + runbooks? I can take lead for next shift.

dave (customer-success): sending targeted message to the 18 affected accounts with current mitigation steps and a temporary workaround (pin to local region). Will escalate any high-urgency customers to SEs.

alice (oncall): handoff: I need to step away in 25m. Handoff to carol (sre). Current status: mitigations applied (prefer-local, reduced retries), GCP has ticket and acknowledged the API anomaly, customers notified. Severity: Sev 2 (customer-impacting multi-customer).

carol (sre): taking over. I'll coordinate live with GCP support and keep the page hot if escalation required. Action items I'm owning:
- liaise with GCP to confirm root cause and ETA for forwarding-rules API recovery
- monitor route re-propagation and confirm customer reachability
- prepare rollback for our earlier rollout if evidence points there
- compile timeline for postmortem

bob (network-eng): GCP response: their networking API team sees elevated errors in the global forwarding-rules service due to an internal dependency; they are rolling a mitigation. No PR yet to our rollout.

gcp-support-bot: Update on 1234567890: Engineering deploying mitigation to global controlplane, estimate 20–40m to stabilize.

carol (sre): starting controlled verification steps:
- run synthetic probes for sample affected customers
- watch for route table changes in impacted projects
- if re-propagation stalls after 15m, prepare plan B (traffic migration + DNS TTL slide)

alice (oncall): FYI post-handoff: I've left a note in the runbook and updated the incident channel. Logged my debugging outputs to /incidents/2190012345/artifacts.txt.

dave (customer-success): customer update: sending ETA based on GCP mitigation window (20–40m) and our temporary fallbacks. Flagging 2 customers for priority SE response.

eve (infra): also adding additional observability: turn on packet-path debug for two impacted ILBs and forward logs to SRE team. Might add noise but useful for root cause.

carol (sre): GCP just confirmed mitigation applied; partial recovery observed in controlplane metrics. I'm seeing decreased 503s ~ 75% drop in last 10m.

bob (network-eng): route propagation tests: 12 / 18 customers show restored cross-region routes, 6 still pending. Those 6 are queued in GCP requeue with guidance from their API team.

carol (sre): continuing watch. If remaining customers don't stabilize in 30m, we'll initiate DNS TTL slide + manual failover for affected prefixes.

gcp-support-bot: Final update: forwarding-rules API global service restored. Monitoring for 2 hours recommended. Ticket 1234567890 will remain open until post-recovery verification.

carol (sre): marking incident as recovering. Postmortem owner: carol. Next steps: collect timelines, correlate our controlplane retries with GCP errors, review retry/backoff policy, and consider exponential backoff defaults for forwarding-rules API.

dave (customer-success): customer comms updated to reflect resolution and monitoring window. No escalations received after initial notices.

alice (oncall): back from break, verified channel. Good work. Recommend follow-ups: audit our early rollout to ensure no correlated increase in controlplane traffic, add a runbook step to immediately toggle prefer-local routing for Private VPC projects, and add alert linking to GCP statuspage for future similar issues.

carol (sre): we'll schedule a postmortem meeting tomorrow and tag eng-network, infra, and cs. Closing incident thread in 2h after monitoring window completes.

bob (network-eng): note for postmortem: gather sample API traces, stack traces for retries, and a list of affected customers + mitigation times.

incident-bot: Incident set to recovering. Incident-TS: 2190012345. Severity: Sev2 -> Recovering. Postmortem: carol (owner).

carol (sre): thanks everyone. I'll drop a brief timeline in #postmortems once we have artifacts. :thumbsup:
